question: A day-4 heel-prick filter-paper TSH result comes back at 42 mIU/L (cut-off >20). The infant appears clinically normal. What is the MOST appropriate immediate next step?

answers.text: Reassure the parents and repeat the screen at 6 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A TSH above the cut-off requires confirmatory serum testing and NOT deferral to 6 weeks — congenital hypothyroidism must be treated early to prevent intellectual disability.

answers.text: Obtain serum TSH and free T4, and start levothyroxine BEFORE imaging results are available

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Confirmatory serum TSH + fT4 should be drawn immediately; levothyroxine is started BEFORE thyroid imaging, because treatment delay worsens neurodevelopmental outcome.

answers.text: Order a thyroid isotope scan first and wait for the result before starting treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Imaging helps determine aetiology but must NEVER delay treatment. Start levothyroxine once serum confirmation is available, regardless of scan timing.

answers.text: Refer to a tertiary centre and await specialist opinion before any intervention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Referral is appropriate but treatment must not be withheld pending specialist review. The primary care physician should initiate levothyroxine at 10–15 mcg/kg/day after serum confirmation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: an elevated newborn screen TSH requires prompt serum confirmation and early levothyroxine. Never wait for imaging or a specialist visit before starting treatment.

Excellent. The cardinal rule of congenital hypothyroidism management: confirm with serum TSH/fT4, then start levothyroxine (10–15 mcg/kg/day) BEFORE imaging — every week of delay matters for brain development.
